chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The angel joyfully ascends with the deed of the servant. So when he ascends with his good deed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Make it in Sijjin, for it is not I whom he intended with it."'

key_terms.سِجِّين: A register or book in which the deeds of the wicked are recorded

ai.seo_question: What happens to good deeds performed for showing off?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of divine acceptance by contrasting the angelic ascent of deeds with God's direct judgment of the servant's inner intent (niyyah). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that even outwardly valid good deeds are relegated to Sijjin if the primary motivation is worldly recognition rather than pure devotion to Allah. This underscores the critical role of sincerity (ikhlas) in determining the spiritual weight of actions.
